result.summary: INV-1 (Tenant data isolation): APPLIES and FAILS. `Letflow.Engine.LuaScriptAudit.execute_script_for_audit/6` writes via `Repo.insert(prefix: opts[:prefix])` with no runtime check that `opts[:prefix]` is present/non-nil before the insert. `AuditRecord` has no `@schema_prefix`, so Ecto's own fallback (`Keyword.get(opts, :prefix, schema.__schema__(:prefix))`, confirmed in deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo/schema.ex:921) resolves to `nil` when a caller omits `:prefix` or passes `prefix: nil`, which writes the row into the connection's default/public schema -- exactly the cross-tenant leak INV-1 exists to prevent. The moduledoc and design doc (req058-lua-script-audit.md, INV-LSA-6) both assert 'no public-schema fallback', but nothing in the code enforces it: no guard clause, no `Keyword.fetch!`, no equivalent of `Letflow.EventStore.append/2`'s own pattern (lib/letflow/event_store.ex:176, `TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix)` inside a `with` chain, which fails closed on a bad/missing prefix before any write). The migration itself is correctly guarded (`if prefix() do`, prefix() on table/index, tenant_provisioning.ex manifest entry present and correctly ordered after 20260820000010) -- (b) passes -- and (c) is N/A (no tenant_id column, consistent with decision 0006 D2). Only (a) -- proof that the write path itself cannot reach public -- fails, and it fails because 'no fallback' is documented intent, not enforced code. INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response/serialization surface added, S4 not started, and this function has no caller yet. INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- diff explicitly excludes the Lua execution runtime itself (Executor is an injected behaviour with no implementation shipped here); S5 has not started. INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES and PASSES -- `grep -rn System.get_env` / hardcoded-secret heuristic against the three changed files returned no hits; no secret material is read, logged, or persisted anywhere in this diff. INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint added. INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES -- this handoff is that proof; verdict tracks INV-1's outcome, so overall FAIL. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): APPLIES and PASSES -- `grep -rn Repo.query` against the three changed files returned zero hits; the only write is `Repo.insert/2` via an `Ecto.Changeset`, parameterised by construction. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES and PASSES -- the sole `{:ok, ...} ->` construct is a `case` clause (line 161), not a bare pattern-match assignment; `execute_script_for_audit/6` uses a `with` chain covering instance-id validation, executor invocation, hash comparison, and insert, with every branch returning a tagged tuple; the executor's `{:error, reason}` result is caught and wrapped rather than crashing.

issues.description: opts[:prefix] is never validated as present/non-nil before the insert. A caller that omits :prefix or passes prefix: nil silently writes the audit row into the default/public Postgres schema instead of failing closed, contradicting this module's own moduledoc and the design doc's INV-LSA-6 claim that there is 'no public-schema fallback'.
issues.required_fix: Add an explicit guard before executor invocation or insert (mirroring lib/letflow/event_store.ex:176's TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) pattern, or at minimum Keyword.fetch(opts, :prefix) with a distinct {:error, :missing_prefix} on :error) so a missing/nil prefix returns a typed error and performs zero writes, instead of silently resolving to the default schema.
